title: Assessment intake playbook for 3rd-party audit log delivery and SIEM export
content:
Purpose:
This playbook describes the intake and delivery process for third-party assessments (penetration tests, red-team engagements, compliance audits) that request audit log exports and SIEM evidence. It standardizes what artifacts we accept, how RBAC and scoped credentials are provisioned, expected audit-log schema, secure delivery paths, automated evidence ingestion hooks, and the triage/remediation workflow. Aim: reduce friction for assessors while preserving data minimization, tenant isolation, and chain-of-custody for evidence.

Audience:
Primary: security assessors, third-party testers, SOC analysts, SRE on-call, infra engineers. Secondary: product owners who own services in scope.

High-level intake flow (summary):
1) Request intake: assessor submits Assessment Request Form (linked_confluence_id) and proposed scope.
2) Scoping call: 30–45 minute call with security lead + service owners to confirm assets, time windows, and data minimization.
3) Scoped credentials & RBAC: short-lived roles created with least privilege; audit logging enabled for those roles.
4) Evidence collection plan: select log buckets, SIEM dashboards, network captures, and retention windows.
5) Delivery & verification: assessor uploads evidence to pre-signed S3 path or pushes to dedicated SIEM export; security validates checksums and schema.
6) Findings & remediation tracking: findings logged in JIRA, severity triaged, owners assigned, and proof-of-fix artifacts collected.

Scope rules (examples we apply):
- Default: production clusters are in-scope only when explicitly requested and approved by a product risk reviewer.
- Sensitive assets (KMS, HSM, private customer PII stores) are out-of-scope unless SOC and Legal approve with extra controls.
- Timeboxed access: all privileged roles provisioned for tests expire within the engagement window + 24 hours.

RBAC provisioning pattern (short-lived, auditable):
- Create a scoped role: sec:assessment/<engagement-id>/<service>-readonly
- Grant only: list/read on logging endpoints, read on S3 evidence buckets, list/get on service metadata endpoints. No write/config privileges.
- Ensure actions are covered by audit logging (see schema fields below).
- Attach an inline policy: require mfa_session and source_ip list.
- Annotate role with tags: engagement_id, assessor, requested_by, purpose.

Audit log schema (canonical fields we require for acceptance):
- timestamp (ISO8601 UTC)
- event_id (uuid)
- principal_id (string) // user or service principal that initiated the event
- principal_type (user | svc | role)
- action (string) // e.g., "iam:AssumeRole", "s3:GetObject", "http:POST /v1/generate"
- resource_type (string) // e.g., cluster, instance, s3-bucket, model-serving-route
- resource_id (string) // resource unique id or ARN-like path
- request_id (string) // trace id correlating request across services
- auth_method (string) // api_key | oauth | mTLS | service_token
- ip_address (string)
- user_agent (string)
- region (string)
- outcome (string) // success | failure | denied | throttled
- bytes_in (integer)
- bytes_out (integer)
- duration_ms (integer)
- details (string) // free text or JSON-escaped metadata
- checksum (sha256 hex) // optional but required for delivered files

Notes on schema:
- We accept JSON-lines (newline-delimited JSON) or compressed JSONL (.jsonl.gz). If the assessor proposes CEF/LEEF, they must provide a JSON mapping file.
- Timestamps must be consistent and in UTC; logs missing timestamp or request_id will be rejected.

Naming & delivery conventions for evidence:
- Bucket path: s3://redwood-assessments/<engagement-id>/raw-logs/<service>/<yyyymmdd>/part-00001.jsonl.gz
- Filename manifest: <engagement-id>_manifest.csv (CSV columns: path, checksum, event_count, start_ts, end_ts)
- Required manifest stored alongside artifacts. Manifest must be signed by assessor PGP key OR include a signed webhook event from their upload system.
- For small engagements (<5GB), we allow direct encrypted upload via pre-signed URL. For larger exports, share a presigned multipart upload or use our secure transfer service (scp over bastion with ephemeral key).

SIEM export requirements and parser guidance:
- Preferred ingestion: JSONL with canonical fields above. If pushing into our SIEM (Splunk/Elastic), we provide an ingest token and index name: assessments-<engagement-id>.
- Ingest mappings: map event_id->_id, timestamp->@timestamp, principal_id->user.name, action->event.action, resource_type->assets.type, resource_id->assets.id, request_id->trace.id, outcome->event.outcome.
- Recommended parser rules: for Elastic ingest, use ingest pipeline with grok/regex for resource_id patterns and set fields with processors (set, rename, convert).
- Example regex for request_id extraction: (?<request_id>[0-9a-fA-F-]{36})
- If assessor provides pre-built CEF events, include a CEF->JSON mapping file and sample converted events for validation.

Automated evidence verification steps (scripted):
1) For each file in manifest: download first 100 lines, validate JSON parse, check presence of required fields.
2) Verify checksum in manifest matches downloaded file.
3) Validate timestamp continuity (no gaps larger than window unless expected).
4) Run sampling rules to ensure RBAC-scoped role actions appear as expected (e.g., role assume events).
5) Run quick SIEM enrichment locally to confirm parser mapping correctness.
6) Create verification report (verification-<engagement-id>.json) and place in evidence/verified/ path.

Sample verification errors we surface to assessors: missing_request_id, invalid_timestamp_format, missing_principal_type, checksum_mismatch, unexpected_write_ops_by_role.

Triage and remediation playbook (for findings from assessments):
- When an assessor submits a finding, security creates a ticket: SEC-<engagement>-<seq>. Ticket fields: title, description, proof_artifact (link), reproduction_steps, expected_behavior, remediation_suggestion, severity, owner, target_fix_date.
- Severity rubric (guideline):
  * Critical: active data exfiltration vector or privilege escalation to infra control plane (TTR 72 hours)
  * High: privilege misuse or path to escalate into critical within 1–2 hops (TTR 7 days)
  * Medium: auth bypass affecting non-sensitive features or noisy denial (TTR 30 days)
  * Low: informational/config recommendations (TTR 90 days)
- Owners: default to service owner listed in ownership registry; if not assigned, default to on-call SRE with escalation to infra-security within 24h.
- Proof-of-fix: require both code/config change plus evidence: new logs showing failed exploit attempts, updated access policy, and updated test case in CI. Attach new evidence to ticket before closing.

Chain-of-custody & privacy notes:
- All delivered evidence is encrypted at rest and access-controlled to tagged roles only.
- Redact customer PII unless explicitly requested and signed off by Legal; if redaction is performed, include redaction log and original checksum (kept in escrow).
- Maintain an access audit for who downloaded evidence; rotate keys after each engagement.

Escalation contacts (primary):
- Security lead: Aisha R. Patel (aisha@redwood.com)
- SOC oncall: soc-oncall@redwood.com
- Infra owner: Jason M. Liu (jliu@redwood.com)
- Legal review: Carmen D. Reyes (creyes@redwood.com)

Appendix: quick samples
- Example JSONL event (one line):
{"timestamp":"2024-02-10T18:34:12.123Z","event_id":"8b6a1e3b-1f2a-4c3a-9d6f-111111111111","principal_id":"svc:assessment-proxy","principal_type":"svc","action":"s3:GetObject","resource_type":"s3-bucket","resource_id":"arn:redwood:s3:us-west-2:123456789012:assessments-abc/raw-logs/service-a/20240210/part-00001.jsonl.gz","request_id":"d4f3c2b1-0000-4a2b-9f6a-abcd12345678","auth_method":"service_token","ip_address":"52.23.45.67","user_agent":"aws-sdk-go/1.34","region":"us-west-2","outcome":"success","bytes_in":0,"bytes_out":1024,"duration_ms":45,"details":"GET object for evidence part","checksum":"e3b0c44298fc1c149afbf4c8996fb92427ae41e4649b934ca495991b7852b855"}

- Minimal manifest CSV (header + example):
path,checksum,event_count,start_ts,end_ts
s3://redwood-assessments/eng-2024-02/raw-logs/service-a/20240210/part-00001.jsonl.gz,e3b0c442...,100000,2024-02-10T00:00:00Z,2024-02-10T23:59:59Z

Operational caveats and known limitations:
- We do NOT allow direct database dumps unless Legal approves. Instead, we provide query-executed extracts with auditor-approved filters.
- Very high-volume logs (>1TB) need advance notice for staging; plan backup retention and transfer windows.
- Some old services produce non-canonical logs; for those we require a mapping file and a short adapter script from the assessor.

Change log (quick):
- 2024-01-15: initial draft with canonical schema and intake flow (created by Aisha).
- 2024-02-05: added manifest signing option and pre-signed multipart guidance (Jason).
- 2024-03-02: clarified RBAC tag naming and SIEM ingest mapping (Evan).

End of playbook. For intake form and scheduling link see Confluence:SEC-INTAKE-87 and contact the security rotation to request a scoping call.
content_summary: Playbook for third-party assessment intake covering audit-log exports, RBAC, delivery, verification, SIEM mapping, and remediation workflow.
notes: Keep original artefacts and checksums; prefer JSONL with canonical schema.
